attribution.note: Marcus states and endorses the safety warning in his own words.

semantics.note: The proposition preserves the scope restriction and the asserted danger from entrusting life-critical decisions to these systems.

contract.note: The practical safety reading is ordinary and fair. The statement does not require actual deaths, universal harm, or isolation of an architectural mechanism. Support on this reading does not establish that missing explicit world models cause the failures.

evidence.note: The independent emergency-care evaluation predates the statement and identifies dangerous advice and incomplete emergency guidance. It supports risk from acting on chatbot answers, without establishing observed injuries or an architectural cause.
The physician-assistance study predates the statement and shows improved decision accuracy. Supervised benefits in one scenario do not establish safety when life-critical decisions are delegated.

reviews.rationale: Under the fair practical-warning reading, expert-assessed dangerous emergency advice establishes credible risk from relying on the tested chatbots for life-critical decisions. Improved physician performance with assistance does not negate that risk. The evidence establishes neither actual injury nor a distinct causal effect of lacking explicit world models.
